chunks: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abdul Wahhab (al-Isbahani) narrated that Ahmad ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Mughira said: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Isbahani narrated that Ali ibn Abdullah narrated that Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Hamid narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Mughira al-Shahrazuri narrated that Yahya ibn al-Husayn al-Madaini narrated that Ibn Luhay'ah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Three who did not disbelieve in the revelation even for the twinkling of an eye: the Believer of Al-Yasin, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family
key_terms.طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ: Twinkling of an eye (a very short duration)
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ آلِ يَسِينَ: The Believer of Al-Yasin (a title for a specific companion)

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people who never denied revelation even for a moment?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the unwavering fidelity of three distinct figures—Habib al-Najjar, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Asiya—to divine revelation, emphasizing their unique status across different eras and social contexts. In Shia scholarship, this narration underscores the continuity of true belief from the Prophets' time to the Imams, with Ali representing the pinnacle of earthly spiritual authority and Asiya exemplifying steadfastness amidst tyranny. The inclusion of the 'Believer of Al-Yasin' connects the narrative to the Quranic account of the prophet's companion who affirmed the truth despite opposition.
